thread:
sam: Heads-up—ran a long nsys sweep against the 8xA100 pool for the new triton selector changes. Seeing repeated 120–250ms stalls tied to JIT compile activity on the 2k seq path. attaching timeline snips below.

marta: ugh. is that during steady-state or only first few requests?

sam: steady-ish. this is not pure cold-start; the spikes show up after a few minutes of traffic. nvprof/nsys shows a compile job kicked off while we had inflight batches.

yang: can you paste the nsys summary? even a short flame slice helps.

sam: pasted: 
```
GPU0: time=00:12:34.512 events: jit_compile 214ms @ 00:11:22.312 (kcache miss), kernel_launch wait 28ms, memcpyHtoD 5ms
GPU1: time=00:12:36.001 events: jit_compile 182ms @ 00:11:23.125 (template_codegen), cuBLAS_matmul 22ms
```

marta: interesting that both GPUs show it. could be our global kernel cache eviction policy. we recently lowered kcache size to reduce RAM pressure.

nidhi: hypothesis: consecutive model variants (fp16 vs q4) trigger separate kernel variants so selector calls compile for the other variant when it sees a new seq length distribution. think we need to instrument selector decisions.

leo: +1 on selector metrics. also check batching heuristics: if dynamic batcher produces a large batch at an unlucky moment, it will kick off a heavy compile for fused attention variant. can we repro with a synthetic trace?

sam: I repro'd with a replay: send 12 requests with seq lengths [512, 512, 1024, 2048, 2048, 128, 2048, 2048, 1024, 512, 2048, 2048] at ~30qps. compile spikes correlate with the first 2048 batch.

yang: can you dump the kernel cache stats around that time? we log hits/misses per-device but not variant-level keys.

sam: current logs: 
```
[11:22:30] kcache: hits=1242 misses=18 evictions=6 size=512MB
[11:22:31] kcache: misses=19 (variant: attn_fused_seq2048_fp16)
[11:22:32] compile: start id=0x7f9 compile_time_ms=214 artifacts=12
```

marta: 18–19 misses is small but each miss is expensive. are we async-compiling? looks like compile ran on the render thread and blocked the worker.

nidhi: we have two modes: sync (blocking) and async (background). the selector change accidentally left a codepath doing sync fallback when variant_key included tensor_layout flag.

leo: that would explain showing up only after some selector tweak. fix: ensure that compile is offloaded to a low-priority compile pool and return fallback kernel while compiling.

sam: I instrumented compile pool usage: compile_pool.queue_len spiked to 0 (i.e., sync) at 11:22:31. So codepath is sync. patch ready to route to async pool and emit telemetry.

yang: other angle: kernel cache churn. if we evict the fused kernels to save 200MB, we pay 200ms per miss. cost model change: avoid evicting fusion artifacts unless >24h unused.

marta: agree. longer TTL for fusion artifacts. but we also need to keep memory cap. maybe we keep a pinned set for top-N most-used fused kernels. cache scoring by recent QPS + compile_cost_ms.

nidhi: added scoring stub in PR: score = hit_rate * 0.7 + compile_cost_ms_normalized * 0.3; will push.

sam: aside: per-nsys timeline, I also see CPU-side stall while triton process does codegen. syscall stack: 
```
#0  clone
#1  futex_wait
#2  pthread_mutex_lock
#3  triton::Codegen::emit
#4  triton::Jit::compile
```

leo: that stack suggests we blocked a common mutex used by the inference threads. we should avoid holding codegen locks in the hot path.

marta: can we patch to pre-reserve codegen metadata and do codegen off-thread without touching hot locks?

yang: yes, precompute templates and do final linking async. also test with --triton-prewarm to see baseline.

sam: ran prewarm flag: compile spikes drop to <30ms but total mem goes up ~60MB per GPU. tradeoff seems fine for production.

nidhi: is there a case where we can't prewarm due to variant explosion (layout x precision x seq len)? we need a heuristic to choose which variants to prewarm.

leo: pick variants with high probability under workload sampler and predicted cost > 50ms. we can reuse the eval traces for that distribution.

yang: action items: 1) patch selector to always route compile to async pool (nidhi) 2) change kcache TTL/pinning (marta + leo) 3) add variant-level kcache metrics and export to console (sam) 4) run 24h soak with prewarm on canary (yang).

sam: I'll open a short PR for the async compile route and attach nsys snippet in the PR description. expect deploy to staging later today.

marta: thanks—please include microbench results (median/95/99) for seq=2048 in the PR.

perf-bot: perf run queued: job=pr-compile-async, env=staging, profile=nsys, duration=30m

nidhi: note for the run: include a suffix test that toggles kcache_size to 1GB vs 256MB to measure delta.

sam: noted. I'll also add an option to dump the selector key per-req to help debug future misses.

leo: sweet. once we have metrics we can set a cost-threshold auto-pinning rule.

marta: if anyone hits the batcher causing compile, add a quick mitigation flag: max_batch_size_for_compile=64 to reduce batch-induced variant compilation for large fused kernels.

sam: thanks all — will update thread when staging spikes confirmed gone or persist. :thumbsup:
